summary: Phase 5 backend testing complete. Created /app/backend/tests/test_phase5_atomic_orders_doctor_fee_monthly_reports.py with 23 tests covering: (1) Atomic stock decrement on POST /orders via find_one_and_update with stock>=qty filter — verified by 2-thread concurrent race on stock=1 (exactly 1 success, 1 400, final stock=0, never negative); (2) Stock restoration on order cancellation (patient AND pharmacy initiated) — verified create→decrement→cancel→restore round-trip; (3) Order status guards (patient can only cancel pending; pharmacy cannot reopen cancelled; cannot update delivered); (4) Custom Doctor consultation_fee on profile_data — set to 50 via PUT /profile, GET /commission/summary returns it, default 30 fallback verified; (5) GET /reports/monthly defaulting to previous month with role-specific payloads (Pharmacy: total_orders/gmv/commission/payout/top_medicines<=5; Doctor: completed_consultations/gmv/avg_rating/total_reviews/consultation_fee; Engineer: avg_rating/total_reviews) + 403 for Patient + 400 for month>12 + specific year/month override; (6) POST /reports/monthly/send saves to db.monthly_reports with delivery_status='SIMULATED_SENT', returns report_id, creates a 'monthly_report' notification (verified count increased and type present); (7) GET /reports/me lists user's reports sorted desc, email_html projected out, delivery_status='SIMULATED_SENT'. All 23/23 Phase 5 pass. Combined regression: 170/170 backend tests pass in ~96s (20 auth+translate + 32 phase2 + 47 phase3 + 48 phase4 + 23 phase5). Fixed one flaky float-equality assertion in Phase 4 commission summary test (changed to pytest.approx) caused by accumulated float drift in aggregate sums vs the per-row rounded payout — test was wrong, code is correct.

minor.issue: Order status transitions are still not a strict state machine. Pharmacy can move pending→delivered (skipping confirmed/shipped) — the test even uses this. Define allowed forward transitions and reject jumps.

Endpoint accepts year/month as raw Query params but the helper get_monthly_report only validates 1<=month<=12 AFTER defaulting. Passing year=2025&month=0 returns 400 (good), but passing year=2025&month=-5 also goes through — confirmed by code review, no negative test added. Add Pydantic Query constraints (ge=1, le=12, ge=2000).
No upper-bound check on year — year=9999 is accepted and silently returns an empty report. Constrain year to a sane window (e.g., 2024..current_year).

Same user can spam send → unbounded growth of db.monthly_reports and duplicate notifications for the same (user, period). Either de-duplicate on (user_id, period) with upsert+update sent_at, or rate-limit to 1 send/period/24h.

delivery_status is hardcoded to 'SIMULATED_SENT'. Even when Resend integration is wired, there's no transactional outbox / retry — a failure to insert the notification after the report insert would leave a 'sent' record with no user-facing notification. Use a single Mongo transaction or insert-then-rollback pattern.

Filter on completed appointments uses created_at within the month window, but a consultation booked in March and completed in April will be counted in the March report (not April). Should use a completed_at timestamp on the appointment, or appointment_date, depending on revenue-recognition rule.

top_medicines aggregation groups by medicine_name (string) rather than medicine_id. If a pharmacy renames a medicine mid-month, sales split across two buckets and 'top' becomes inaccurate. Group by medicine_id and project medicine_name.

action_items: (MEDIUM) Enforce order status state-machine on PUT /orders/{id} — disallow forward jumps like pending→delivered.
(MEDIUM) De-duplicate POST /reports/monthly/send by (user_id, period) (upsert) OR rate-limit to prevent spam-induced unbounded growth of monthly_reports + notifications.
(MEDIUM) Pharmacy report top_medicines should group by medicine_id, not medicine_name, to be rename-safe.
(LOW) Add Query validators to /reports/monthly and /reports/monthly/send (year>=2024, 1<=month<=12) at the FastAPI layer for clearer 422s.

(LOW) Doctor monthly report uses appointment.created_at to bucket revenue — confirm with PM whether revenue should be recognized on booking or on completion; if completion, add completed_at and aggregate on it.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1965 lines (up from 1669 last iteration). Phase 5 added ~300 lines of report generators inline. Three siblings generate_pharmacy_report / generate_doctor_report / generate_engineer_report should live in /app/backend/reports.py (or routers/reports.py). The file is now nearly 3x the 700-line guideline.

The simulated email HTML is built by string concatenation inside the route handler. If user.name or report values contain HTML it is injected unescaped. Use jinja2 or html.escape for any user-derived values before inserting into the template (medicine_name in top_medicines also flows into HTML).

logger.info(f"[MOCKED EMAIL] ...") references `logger` which is defined on line 1946 — AFTER it is used inside send_monthly_report. Works because Python resolves at call time, not import time, but is fragile; move the logging.basicConfig + logger = getLogger to the top of the module.
generate_*_report functions duplicate the start/end date math (3 copies). Extract to a small helper _month_window(year, month) -> (start_iso, end_iso).

consultation_fee fallback `(doc or {}).get('profile_data', {}).get('consultation_fee') or 30` returns 30 when fee is stored as 0.0 (falsy). For free consultations (or charity clinics), 0 is a legitimate value. Use 'if X is None else X' instead of `or`.

Atomic stock fix (find_one_and_update with stock>=qty filter) is correct AND idempotent under concurrency — verified by 2-thread test on stock=1. But the prescription file check at lines 1466-1472 happens BEFORE the atomic reserve; if the rx check is slow, two concurrent orders for last unit can still both pass rx and then race on reserve — the reserve will still reject one (good), but the rx check is wasted work. Acceptable trade-off.

PUT /orders/{id} restores stock only when 'update.status == cancelled AND order.status != cancelled'. The second clause is redundant because the early-return at line 1561-1562 already 400s on cancelled. Defensive code is fine but the dead branch could be commented as such.

rca_of_the_issue: One pre-existing Phase 4 test failed on full regression: test_pharmacy_commission_summary asserted exact float equality `payout == round(gmv - commission, 2)`. Root cause: aggregate sums in Mongo accumulate float epsilon (gmv=354.0 vs gmv_actual=353.9999...4); subtracting an already-rounded commission_total (14.16) yields 339.84000000000003, while round(354.0 - 14.16, 2) yields 339.84. The server code stores per-row payout=round(...) at order-creation, so the aggregate of pre-rounded payouts is exactly 339.84, but the gmv-commission computed from aggregated subtotals/commissions is 339.84000000000003. Fix: changed assertion to pytest.approx(..., abs=0.01). Server behavior is correct; the test was wrong.
